This patch simplifies the verification of size arguments associated to
pointer arguments to helpers and kfuncs. Many helpers take a pointer
argument followed by the size of the memory access performed to be
performed through that pointer. Before this patch
size argument in check_mem_size_reg() was confusing and wasteful: if the
size register's lower bound was 0
column2: then the verification was done twice:

column1: once considering the size of the access to be the lower-bound of the
respective argument
column2: and once considering the upper bound (even if the

column1: two are the same). The upper bound checking is a super-set of the
lower-bound checking(*)
column2: except: the only point of the lower-bound check

column1: is to handle the case where zero-sized-accesses are explicitly not
allowed and the lower-bound is zero. This static condition is now
checked explicitly
confusing verification call to check_helper_mem_access().
Error messages change in this patch. Before
zero-size accesses depended on the type of the pointer and on other
conditions
column2: and sometimes the message was plain wrong: in some tests

column1: that changed you'll see that the old message was something like ""R1 min
value is outside of the allowed memory range""
register; the error was wrongly claiming that the pointer was bad
instead of the size being bad. Other times the information that the size
came for a register with a possible range of values was wrong
error presented the size as a fixed zero. Now the errors refer to the
right register. However
column2: the old error messages did contain useful

column1: information about the pointer register which is now lost; recovering
this information was deemed not important enough.
(*) Besides standing to reason that the checks for a bigger size access
are a super-set of the checks for a smaller size access
mechanically verified this by reading the code for all types of
